title: resolve-review-loop contract
description: Single source of truth for the always-emitted review-loop resolver contract. Every field here is emitted by scripts/resolve-review-loop.sh on a default run AND validated by src/engine/resolve-review-loop.js. src/engine/resolve-review-loop.js DERIVES its REVIEW_LOOP_FIELDS list and its assertOneOf enum tables from this document — do not hand-maintain a second copy. scripts/check-contract-schema.js gates the shell side against it. Conditional/optional keys (reviewer_qualified, fallback_ladder, verify_first, capability_tier, density_scaled, density_source) are emitted only under specific flags and are NOT part of this always-on contract; they are handled separately in the JS validator. x-field-order fixes the canonical REVIEW_LOOP_FIELDS ordering. x-shell-validated marks the enum fields whose allowed-value set the shell resolver enforces via a case statement; x-shell-var names the shell variable whose case arm enforces it (check-contract-schema.js reconciles the per-field arm).

implementer_ladder.description: Optional ordered implementer rungs. Each item is engine/effort@runner. Empty when the field is absent: the three implementer_* fields are the single implicit rung. Availability fallback remains on_engine_unavailable.

reviewer_engine_low_risk.description: Risk-tiered overlay: non-empty (with reviewer_effort_low_risk) = the LOOP reviewer engine for computed review_risk=low; empty = tiering off (reviewer_engine used at every risk). High risk always uses reviewer_engine.

reviewer_effort_low_risk.description: Effort for reviewer_engine_low_risk: empty or low|medium|high|xhigh|max. Shell coerces garbage to empty (tiering off — fail-safe reviews with the stronger incumbent). Deliberately NOT x-shell-validated: the parity gate models exact-set enums, and this field's set includes the empty string.

on_family_conflict.description: Engine reviewDiff policy when the (effective) reviewer shares the implementer's model family: fallback = substitute the first cross-family qualified row from fallback_ladder (runner-allowlisted, fail-closed on no candidate); block = hard-block (pre-v2.32.25 behavior). Resolver coerces garbage to block; the engine treats absent/invalid as block. The conditional --check-scorecard key fallback_ladder_implementer_family carries ladder provenance (the implementer family the ladder was computed against) so a stale pre-resolved roster fails closed.

reviewer_fallback_preference.description: HUMAN-ordered engine ids the engine's family-conflict fallback prefers over raw ladder order; every candidate still passes all fallback guards. Empty = ladder order.

reviewer_fallback_preference_low_risk.description: Preference list applied when computed review_risk=low; empty = use reviewer_fallback_preference.

qc_panel_seats.description: Exact readiness identity for every QC seat. Empty with qc_panel_seats_complete=false means the legacy model-only panel lacks enough metadata; consumers must fail closed rather than guess.

plan_review.description: Enable the first-class bounded plan-readiness rail. Independent from the deprecated spec_review implementation-loop switch.

strict_l5_policy_override.description: Non-empty = deliberate, recorded escape from strict /l5 byte-equal policy coverage; the string is the operator's reason and is surfaced on every derivation. Empty = fail-closed (default).

brain_seat.description: Brain-seat standing on the P7-governed paths (plan 2026-08-17-brain-seat-exam-suite P4). null = no seat context configured. Candidate seats without standing are refused; the incumbent annotates loudly (Board 2026-08-16 advisory bootstrap semantics); the per-invocation override admits with an EVIDENCE-FREE warning — never a silent third path.

consult_engine.description: Engine for a mid-run ad-hoc heterogeneous second opinion (the "consult" role). Empty = no configured consult seat; the caller hand-types dispatch-review.sh argv as before. Tuple rule: engine/runner/effort are wholly empty or all three present.

consult_runner.description: Runner for the consult seat. Empty when the seat is unconfigured. Deliberately NOT x-shell-validated: check-contract-schema.js models exact-set enums and this set includes the empty string (same reason reviewer_effort_low_risk is excluded). The shell enforces the identical set via its own case arm.

discuss_engine.description: Engine for heterogeneous participation in dialectic/ideation skills (think-tank, brainstorm) — the "discuss" role. Empty = no configured discuss seat. NO EXECUTABLE CONSUMER READS THIS YET (see docs/scripts-inventory.md and the run summary): it is a declared seat awaiting a caller, not a live route.

discuss_runner.description: Runner for the discuss seat. Empty when the seat is unconfigured. Deliberately NOT x-shell-validated: check-contract-schema.js models exact-set enums and this set includes the empty string (same reason reviewer_effort_low_risk is excluded). The shell enforces the identical set via its own case arm.

consult_dispatch.description: Whether the consult rail (scripts/dispatch-consult.sh) is live. DEFAULT OFF. off = today's behavior exactly — the consult_* seat tuple stays data a caller may read by hand, no new dispatch. on requires a non-empty consult seat tuple (empty seat + on is a misconfiguration) and, once D7 lands, a role-qualification row or matching override for that seat.

discuss_dispatch.description: Whether the discuss rail (scripts/dispatch-discuss.js) is live. DEFAULT OFF. off = today's behavior exactly — discuss_* stays declared but not consumed. on requires a non-empty discuss seat tuple and, once D7 lands, a role-qualification row or matching override for that seat.

allow_same_runner_dual_seat.description: Board ruling 2026-08-27, scope corrected by the depth-0 QC panel. DEFAULT OFF. Governs whether one runner may occupy the implementer seat AND a reviewer-class LOOP seat (reviewer / reviewer_low_risk / verification_author / plan_reviewer / plan_deep_reviewer / consult / discuss) in the same roster. off = the resolver exits 3. on = permitted, with a stderr warning and same_runner_dual_seat: true. It applies to QUALIFIED engines too — the rationale 'one vendor, one auth, one server-side prompt layer is not decorrelation' has no qualified-engine exemption. The axis is the RUNNER, not the model family: one rail can serve several families (a single cursor rail hosts both GPT and Grok ids), so a family test would miss exactly the case the ruling names. Comparison is over the CONFIGURED runner token, and 'auto' is inert — it delegates the choice rather than asserting a rail, which is what keeps the shipped template (implementer auto, reviewer codex) valid. An inherited built-in default DOES count: a roster naming only implementer_runner: codex collides with the default reviewer codex, because the resolved loop really does put one rail on both sides. The terminal qc_panel is NOT governed by this key — it is a multi-seat body with union-on-verified-critical aggregation, so it has its own proportionate rule: only TOTAL overlap (every engine-bearing seat on the implementer runner) is refused, and partial overlap is silent by design.

same_runner_dual_seat.description: FACT, not policy: true when one runner actually occupies both the implementer seat and a reviewer-class LOOP seat, OR when EVERY usable qc_panel seat runs on the implementer runner. Emitted so the run summary can report reduced decorrelation without re-deriving it. For loop seats the condition is only reachable when allow_same_runner_dual_seat is on (off exits 3). For the qc_panel only TOTAL overlap counts — every seat carrying BOTH an engine and a runner sitting on the implementer own rail, i.e. no runner decorrelation anywhere in the terminal gate — and that also exits 3 unless deliberately opened. PARTIAL panel overlap is deliberately neither flagged nor warned: the shipped default panel spans three rails on purpose, so one overlapping seat is the recommended configuration, and the pre-existing cross-family control already reports panel/implementer family sharing.

override_admitted_seats.description: Seat roles (e.g. "reviewer", "consult", "qc_panel[1]") whose runner has NO recorded role qualification and was admitted ONLY by a matching AUTOPILOT_QUALIFICATION_OVERRIDE entry. Empty on every qualified roster. This is the recorded-operator-decision surface Board ruling 1 requires — it is NOT evidence of qualification, and nothing downstream may read it as such. ADR-0001: an override is a recorded decision re-derived from the override file on every resolve, never an attestation.
